title: Quarterly Canary Bake & Fiscal Guardrails for Dedicated Pool Autoscale
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: establish a quarterly cadence to bake canary experiments and financial guardrails for Dedicated pool autoscale so that we can safely increase burst capacity without surprising unit economics or violating SLOs. This ticket scopes the roadmap for Q2 2026 covering: experiment definition, test harnesses, budget telemetry, rollback criteria, and cross-org runbooks. The goal is to graduate two canaries (warm-pool behavior and spot-to-dedicated fallback) to production-ready runbooks by end of quarter.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Two end-to-end canary experiments defined with hypothesis, dataset, and traffic shaping. 2) Test harness running in dedicated-sandbox with telemetry capture (cost, p95 latency, error-rate, queue depth). 3) Automated rollback policy implemented and exercised via chaos test. 4) Financial guardrail dashboard shows projected unit cost delta and alerts when threshold exceeded. 5) Ops runbook and run-deck published to Confluence with paging/playbook links.
milestones: M2: Canary 1 (warm-pool prewarm) executed in sandbox - 2026-04-20
M4: Production rollouts and runbook handoff - 2026-06-15
success_metrics: Decrease average cold-start latency by >=15% for dedicated pools during surge windows
Unit cost change measured and bounded within +5% target guardrail
Number of incidents attributable to autoscale regressions = 0 during rollout week
Canary-to-prod rollback exercised at least once in staging
risks: Telemetry blindspots for cross-region cache warming
Incorrect traffic shaping causes noisy signals and false positives
Billing lag causes delayed guardrail triggers
Resource contention with other Dedicated initiatives during peak season
rollout_plan: Phase A: sandbox canaries with 10% synthetic traffic (Ops + Eng observers). Phase B: limited real-customer traffic (1% requests across two low-risk accounts) with circuit-breaker. Phase C: gradual ramp (1%->10% over 48 hours) and full handoff once metrics stable for 72 hours. Each phase requires sign-off by SRE, Finance, and Product.
